newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SOC DEMS SURGE PAST PM'S PARTY AS VOTE NEARS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SOC DEMS SURGE PAST PM'S PARTY AS VOTE NEARS.

text.p: The leading Czech opposition Social Democratic Party (CSSD) has overtaken Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's ODS party in a popularity poll just five weeks before nationwide Senate elections, a poll released on Monday showed.

The September poll, conducted by private Factum agency, said 24.4 percent of the 2,073 potential voters surveyed would support Senate candidates from the centre-left CSSD, while 23.7 percent would vote for Klaus's centre-right Civic Democratic Party (ODS).
It is the first time since pre-Senate election polls began in July that the CSSD has led the ODS, Factum said.
Elections for the Senate, the upper house of the Czech parliament, will be held for the first time in the country's history on November 15-16, under a first past-the-post system in 81 constituencies.

The vote will be the first test of the newly-aligned Czech political landscape after elections to the lower house deprived Klaus's coalition of its majority and made the CSSD the second biggest party.

The survey also showed that the Social Democrats would erase ODS' 3.3 percent August lead in preferences for the lower house of parliament, the Chamber of Deputies, if elections were held immediately, a trend other recent polls have also shown.
But the poll suggests that the ruling coalition, including ODS, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) and the Christian- Democratic Union (KDU-CSL), would take a majority in the 200-seat lower house.
In June, the coalition lost its majority in general elections, winning only 99 seats in the proportional representation system used for the lower house.
The poll also showed the far-right Republican Party (SPR-RSC) would not pass the five percent treshold necessary for winning seats in the chamber, after winning 8.0 percent in the last elections.
PREFERENCES (PCT) SEPTEMBER AUGUST JUNE ELECTION RESULT
